body: Runes are the alphabet of your spellbook. Every custom spell is built from rune order, not just rune membership.
Use the rune forge to prepare spells into slots before combat. The forge is where crafting, evolution, and loadout management meet.
Any spell can eventually be evolved into a summon. In this demo build, treat the forge as the center of long-run growth.
guides.title: Spell Crafting

body: Rune affinity rises when you use spells that contain those runes. There is no decay in the current design.
Higher affinity feeds evolution and can later shape spell power, naming, and summon identity.
If you want a build to grow, cast the runes you care about instead of spreading use evenly across the whole pool.
guides.title: Runes And Affinity

body: Exploration is room-based. You choose visible exits instead of moving a character across a tile grid.
Discovery is stored per run. Incomplete maps become dark maps, which are a weaker trade good and may hurt reputation.
Treat the minimap as support. The primary play surface is the current room, its exits, and its active interaction.
guides.title: Maps And Dark Maps

body: Combat is an interaction view, not a top-level mode. It appears only when the room has a hostile focus.
Prepared spells are your combat loadout. Summons are evolved spells and act after your turn once active.
On victory you earn progress and mana-crystal economy pressure relief. On failure or flight, the room loop resumes.
guides.title: Combat And Summons

body: Dungeon time advances in ticks. Movement and rest both move the dungeon clock forward.
Boss pressure and hostile spawns are driven by those ticks, so every room decision trades safety against momentum.
NPCs share the same room graph and the same clock. The dungeon is a race, not a static puzzle.
guides.title: Turn Order

body: Main play uses keyboard and mouse. Journal, Bag, Controls, and room interactions should always be reachable without hidden debug routes.
Journal holds Quests, Bestiary, and Guides. Dialogue is its own interaction path and should not replace the journal.
The KAPLAY demo is the first consumer of the content delivery engine, so UI wording and structure should stay consistent with authored content.
guides.title: Gameplay Controls
